The long-word chunking and the empty-input fix are correct and match the docstring. The old code returned [""] for blank text; it now returns [].

But changing `len(current) + 1 + len(word) <= width` to `< width` contradicts the docstring, which says a word is appended "if the resulting line is at most `width` characters long". The PR description admits the change was made only to make test_meeting_reminder pass. With `<`, joined lines can never reach exactly `width`, which quietly changes behaviour for every caller of this published library (v0.9.0).

The test's expectation looks wrong. At width 20, "The meeting has been" is exactly 20 characters, so the greedy rule in the docstring gives ["The meeting has been", "moved to Thursday at", "noon."]. The teammate said the docstrings are the source of truth and the tests shouldn't be changed, so this conflict needs to go back to them instead of being settled by bending the implementation.

Please restore `<=`, keep the chunking and empty-list fixes, and report that test_meeting_reminder contradicts the documented contract so the team can decide whether to fix the test or the spec.
